chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
“If the thief comes of his own accord, repenting to Allah, and returns what he stole to its owner, then there is no amputation upon him.”

key_terms.تَائِبًا: repenting; returning to Allah in remorse
key_terms.صَاحِبِهَا: its owner; the rightful possessor of the stolen item
key_terms.قَطْعَ: amputation; the prescribed hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.وَرَدَّ: and he returned; restored what had been taken
key_terms.ٱلسَّارِقُ: the thief; the person guilty of theft

ai.seo_question: Does a thief who repents voluntarily and returns the stolen property still face amputation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when a thief voluntarily comes forward in repentance to Allah and restores the stolen property to its owner, the hadd punishment of amputation is not carried out upon him. It highlights both the legal significance of voluntary repentance and the restoration of the rights of others.
